title: Tenant Thermostat: Telemetry-Driven Prewarm & Adaptive Isolation PRD
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem statement and high-level intent: Dedicated customers experience unpredictable latency/failed requests during tenant traffic surges and cold starts. Existing reserved pools and burst mechanics provide coarse-grained protection but don't adapt to rapid telemetry changes or provide safe prewarm budgets tied to historical traffic patterns. This PRD proposes a 'Tenant Thermostat' feature: a telemetry-driven prewarm budgeter plus adaptive isolation epochs that dynamically shape tenant traffic into dedicated pools to preserve SLOs while allowing controlled burst behavior.
background: We currently offer reserved pools, burst windows, and preemption fallbacks. Production incidents in 2025-12 and 2026-01 showed repeated step spikes where tenants hit cold VM syntheses, causing latency SLO violations. SRE proposals called for smarter prewarming and finer-grained tenant shaping rather than static reservation increases. Customers ask for predictable latency during planned spikes (campaigns, demos) and for lower wasted dedicated capacity between spikes.
goals: Reduce P95/P99 latency violations for dedicated customers during sudden tenant surges by 60%
Enable controlled prewarming budgets per tenant based on telemetry and business entitlements
Provide non-disruptive soft-isolation epochs that favor tenant SLOs without wholesale eviction of other tenants
Expose observability for prewarm actions, isolation epochs, and budget consumption in Console
non_goals: Replacing existing reserved pool purchase flow (billing changes handled separately)
Full multi-region migration strategies — scope limited to a single zone rollout
Support for on-prem air-gapped installs in the initial release
requirements: RQ-1: Telemetry aggregation pipeline exposes per-tenant short-window qps, queue length, and warmness score (0..1) every 15s
RQ-2: Prewarm budgeter computes per-tenant prewarm credits using 7d rolling traffic percentiles and entitlement multipliers
RQ-3: Prewarm requests can request 'soft-prewarm' which triggers a warmup allocation with a soft-timeout and does not evict reserved tenants
RQ-4: Adaptive isolation epochs can be triggered automatically when the platform detects a tenant's warmness score falling below threshold and predicted spike > configured burst threshold
RQ-5: Console shows per-tenant prewarm budget, current consumption, epoch state, and an audit trail of automated actions
RQ-6: Admins can configure tenant thermostat parameters (sensitivity, max prewarm per-window, epoch length, operator override) via Console or API
RQ-7: All automated prewarm/isolation actions must be logged to audit trail and surfaced to SSO/SAML-compliant logging for customers with Private deployments
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: System calculates prewarm budgets and applies a warm allocation for a synthetic 10x qps spike in staging without causing >10% eviction of other tenants
AC-2: In e2e load test, P95 latency for target tenant remains within committed SLOs while platform CPU/GPU utilization does not exceed 90% cluster-wide
AC-3: Console UI displays prewarm budget and a time-series of consumption; clicking a budget entry opens an audit entry with timestamp and triggering metric
AC-4: Admin override API accepts a 'force-prewarm' call which increments tenant prewarm credit and returns an operation ID visible in audit logs
AC-5: Metrics dashboard surfaces a prewarm-to-success ratio (started vs successful warmups) and false-positive rate under 5% after 2 weeks of production data
AC-6: SLO regression test in release pipeline validates that rollout of thermostat to 10% of customers does not increase platform-wide P99 by >2ms
metrics: primary: Reduction in P95/P99 latency violations for tenants during spikes (relative %)
secondary: Average prewarm credit consumption per tenant per week
ops: Prewarm action success rate, warm allocation lead time (median seconds), false-positive prewarm rate
cost: incremental GPU-hours attributed to prewarming vs projected savings from avoided SLO breaches
design_constraints_and_tradeoffs: We favor conservative prewarming (lower false positives) in v1 to avoid wasted capacity; that prioritizes SLO preservation over maximal burst coverage. This increases implemented complexity in telemetry models (predictive percentiles) but reduces customer surprise. We will not attempt global cross-zone prewarming in v1 to keep allocation orchestration simple.
ux_and_console_requirements: Console: New Tenant Thermostat panel within Dedicated -> Tenants showing budget, usage, last-trigger reason
Console: Actionable controls: toggle thermostat on/off, set sensitivity slider, set max prewarm per 24h
Notifications: Tenant admins can opt into webhook alerts when prewarm budget is consumed or epoch triggered
rollout_plan: Phase A (staging): Implement telemetry collection and mock prewarm allocations for internal tenants (2 weeks)
Phase B (canary): Enable thermostat for 10% of dedicated tenants with monitoring and kill-switch (4 weeks)
Phase C (gradual ramp): 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 6 weeks with weekly checkpoints
Phase D (opt-in customer pilot): Invite 3 enterprise customers to pilot advanced sensitivity settings and collect feedback
dependencies: ENG-20412: Telemetry pipeline: short-window per-tenant metrics
ENG-20789: Allocation API: warm allocation and soft-timeout hooks
ENG-21100: Console: tenant view & audit timeline components
SEC-3410: Audit log export for Private deployments
implementation_notes: Engineering will implement a conservative rule-based predictor (percentile + recent slope) for v1, with a hook for ML model lookup in v2. Prewarm allocations should be tagged with origin=thermostat and tenant_budget_id for billing/chargeback.
risks_mitigation: Risk: Excessive wasted capacity due to false-positive warmups -> Mitigation: strict upper-bound per-tenant and kill-switch; monitor false-positive metric
Risk: Incorrect telemetry leading to missed prewarms -> Mitigation: fallbacks to manual 'force-prewarm' and post-mortem alerts
Risk: Customer confusion about prewarm charges -> Mitigation: clear Console labels, billing doc, and email notification during pilot
comments_and_updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting — agreed to prioritize conservative prewarm limits and observability over aggressive burst coverage.
2026-03-05: Eng spike validated telemetry availability for warmness score; initial percentile algorithm shows stable signals.

2026-03-12: Blocker identified: allocation API needs soft-timeout flag (ENG-20789) — working with Eng to schedule in Cycle 11
next_steps: Finalize telemetry schema, land ENG-20789 fix, and schedule Phase A deployment to staging with internal tenants by 2026-03-22. Prepare pilot invitation message for 3 enterprise customers and update billing docs to mention prewarm attribution.
